links_touching_record.rationale: FB2-SW-SIR-000002 is the software interface requirement set for the actuation boundary and is specified by FB2-SW-IFS-000003 (contactor actuation and feedback driver). The direction is specification to requirement, which is the direction a requirement is written in: the interface specification establishes what the interface is by analysing the source at the pinned commit, and the requirement states what must be true of it. This is the opposite of the direction the three existing FB2-SW-SWR-* requirements were produced in - those are back-inferred from the implementation and their revision history says so - and naming the relationship explicitly is what keeps the two directions distinguishable. Every statement in the requirement is traceable to a named element of the specification, and the requirement carries that traceability as a field rather than leaving it in prose.

The triage record classifies the disposition of element FB2-SW-SIR-000002-E, which the actuation interface-requirement record states and marks NOT SATISFIED. The triage depends on that record's element statement and its evidence; if the record were wrong about the return type having two members, the disposition of that element would be wrong too. The dependency is declared rather than left implicit, and the triage does not edit the record it triages.

asil_justification.statement: Not applicable, and deliberately so. This requirement carries no safety allocation because the item it describes has not been through a hazard analysis and risk assessment, so there is no severity or exposure rating to derive an ASIL from. No ASIL is asserted for the real product and none is asserted here. This is not a statement that the interface is unimportant: it is a statement that the classification apparatus is not available in this repository, and a reader must not read 'not_applicable' as 'no consequence'.

authority_and_independence.independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent. It is a derivation from an analysed specification, not an elicitation, not an analysis of a higher-level requirement, and not independent review.

derivation.authoring_independence_statement: Authored by an AI agent from the interface specifications and the source. No requirements engineer confirmed that this is the interface that was wanted, no stakeholder stated a need that these requirements answer, and no human approved them. They record what the code obliges a consumer to rely on; they do not record what anyone asked for.
derivation.method: Every statement names the interface element it obliges and the analysed behaviour it rests on.

element_requirements.basis: STD_OK is assigned only after a registry match, and the initial negative value is returned otherwise.
element_requirements.statement: An actuation request shall report whether the request was placed on a configured contactor.

element_requirements.basis: The return value is initialised to the undefined enumerator and returned unchanged on the no-match path.
element_requirements.statement: The state read shall return an explicit indication when no configured contactor matches, rather than a default or stale state.

element_requirements.basis: Two assertions at the top of each element: stringNumber < BS_NR_OF_STRINGS and the type is not CONT_UNDEFINED.
element_requirements.statement: Every actuation request shall reject a string index outside the configured string count and shall reject the undefined contactor type.

element_requirements.basis: Declared void; the body compares the commanded state with the feedback and registers one diagnosis event per contactor.
element_requirements.statement: The feedback check shall deliver its entire effect through the diagnosis module and shall not rely on a return value.

element_requirements.basis: This one is NOT met by the analysed implementation. It is recorded as a requirement precisely because the interface does not provide it: the single negative value is returned on both paths, so a consumer cannot distinguish a configuration error from a transient condition.
element_requirements.statement: An actuation request that matches no configured contactor and an actuation request that matched but could not be completed shall be distinguishable to the caller.

record_verbatim.element_requirements_note: The failure reaction of the actuation boundary is a trap for a bad argument and a silent ambiguity for a refused request. Requirement E has no detection channel at all today: a caller cannot distinguish the two causes of refusal, so a configuration error presents as an intermittent failure. That is stated here because it is the reason E is worth writing down.
record_verbatim.failure_reaction: Requirement E is not satisfied today and this record does not claim it is. It is stated because a requirement that describes what the interface should do is what makes the shortfall actionable; a note in an interface specification is not. Every other requirement in this set is satisfied by the implementation as analysed, and each carries the source line that satisfies it.
not_established_by_this_record: One requirement in this set is not satisfied by the implementation as analysed, and this record says so rather than dropping it. Requirement E would require a distinct return value per cause, which the declared two-value return type cannot express.
No requirement here is elicited from a stakeholder, a system requirement or a safety goal. Each states an obligation the existing code already imposes, except E which states one it does not.

The requirement set does not state the physical or timing contract of an actuation: no contactor rating, no switching time, no feedback settling time. None of those exists in this repository, and the hardware that would carry them is external.
No ASIL, no safety allocation, no conformity claim, no certification, no human approval.
No verification has been performed against any of these requirements and no test measure exists for any of them.
record_verbatim.rationale: The requirements exist because the analysed interface has two properties a consumer must be able to rely on and one it demonstrably lacks. The two are that the string and contactor-type arguments are bounded, and that a state read distinguishes 'no such contactor' from a real state. The third is the gap: the single negative return value is used both for a request that matched nothing and for a request that matched and could not be completed, so a consumer cannot tell a configuration error from a transient condition. Stating that as a requirement rather than leaving it as an observation is what makes the gap visible to a requirements process instead of to whoever happens to read the source.

revision_history.author: sw_engineer
revision_history.description: Four interface requirements over the actuation boundary, derived from FB2-SW-IFS-000003. They record the obligations a consumer of the contactor driver may rely on, including the one the analysed interface does not provide: a distinguishable report of why an actuation request was refused.

safety_allocation.mitigation: No ASIL is allocated to this requirement. It is a software interface requirement about how two modules call each other, and the product it describes has never had a hazard analysis and risk assessment: no ISO 26262 conformity, no ASIL determination and no certification is claimed for it or for anything in this corpus. The non-applicability is stated with its reason rather than left blank, because an unexplained non-applicability is indistinguishable from a requirement that quietly dropped out of every ASIL-derived view.

record_verbatim.statement: The actuation interface shall present the following to its consumers: (a) a request entry point whose result reports whether the request was placed on a configured contactor; (b) a state read that returns an explicit indication when no such contactor exists rather than a stale or default state; (c) a feedback check whose entire effect is delivered through the diagnosis module; and (d) an argument range on every actuation request, bounded by the configured string count and excluding the undefined contactor type.
record_verbatim.title: Software interface requirements: the actuation interface

verification_status.statement: No test measure exists for any requirement in this record, and no requirement in it has been verified against running code. Every derivation below is an inspection of the source at the pinned commit, which is why the verification approach is analysis and why the coverage matrix in the implementation mapping document reports this record as uncovered. That is the accurate position, not a gap to be filled by writing more prose.

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Transcribe a completed signature into the record as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block plus a revision_history entry naming the reviewer and citing this packet, and archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract.
